business_model: On-demand pickup-pack-ship service, per-transaction fee, courier-network-dependent

historical_evidence.company: On-demand shipping startup letting users request pickup of an item via app; Shyp would then pack and ship it on the customer's behalf for a flat service fee plus shipping cost.
historical_evidence.market: Part of the broader 2014-2015 'on-demand economy' wave (alongside similarly structured startups in food, laundry, and other categories), a category that was itself a subject of active, contemporaneous investor debate about unit-economics sustainability.
historical_evidence.team: No widely reported prior-exit or notable-pedigree signal found in the sources reviewed for this snapshot.
historical_evidence.product: Simple, low-friction consumer product (request pickup via app, item gets packed and shipped) expanding city by city; live in four cities (including a newly launched Los Angeles market) as of the snapshot.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised a $50M Series B in April 2015 led by Kleiner Perkins (John Doerr personally led the deal and joined the board), at a $250M valuation, bringing total funding to $62.2M — a strong signal of top-tier investor conviction. ENRICHED (see benchmark_notes): a real, dated pre-snapshot expansion timeline is now established — Shyp launched in Miami in November 2014 (its third market after San Francisco and New York) and was already preparing a Los Angeles launch for 'early 2015' at that time, meaning the LA beta live as of the April 2015 snapshot represents the completion of a roughly five-month-old expansion plan rather than a sudden, unplanned move — real evidence of deliberate, sequenced geographic-expansion execution, not just a funding-size signal.
historical_evidence.traction: No specific transaction-volume, repeat-usage, or revenue figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed.
historical_evidence.financial: The per-transaction, courier-dependent, physically-fulfilled service model (pickup + packing labor + shipping cost, for a single flat customer fee) was a structurally margin-thin model that was part of the broader, contemporaneously-active 'is the on-demand economy's unit economics sustainable' debate in 2015 tech press covering this wave of startups generally, though no Shyp-specific unit-economics figures were found.

normalized_facts.value: Shyp's third market, after San Francisco and New York
